chunks: They bartered their lives ill denying the revelation of God out of spite that God should bestow His grace among His votaries on whomsoever He will, and thus earned wrath upon wrath. The punishment for disbelievers is ignominious.
ai.seo_question: Why did the disbelievers barter their souls for disbelief according to this verse?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse highlights the psychological root of disbelief as 'baghyā' (envy or ambition), where the elite of the People of the Book rejected Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) not due to lack of evidence, but to preserve their own status against the divine choice of the humble. The phrase 'ghadab 'alā ghadab' (wrath upon wrath) is interpreted as a dual punishment: one for their initial rejection of the truth and a second for their stubbornness in maintaining it despite clear signs. This underscores the Shia emphasis on the merit of the Ahl al-Bayt, who were chosen by God despite their lack of worldly power, contrasting with those who sought dominance.
